note:
SEVEN CONSTRAINTS IN account_report.py NOW SPELL THEMSELVES _check_. 153 -> 146.

Measured in detached worktrees of HEAD, one clean and one holding only this change:

  clean worktree of HEAD   153   -- against a committed floor of 151
  the same worktree + this 146

The two units between the committed 151 and the 153 HEAD measures are not this
change's: the gate was already failing in the rising direction before it, and the
scanner records counts rather than provenance, so they are absorbed here without
an attribution rather than guessed at.

The seven that are this change's are the @api.constrains methods on account.report
and account.report.line, which used both conventions for one job -- three were
already _check_parent_line / _check_carryover_target / _check_formula while seven
others were _validate_*. §2.4 reserves _check_ for constraints and every one of
these is one:

  _validate_root_report_id         -> _check_root_report_id
  _validate_parent_sequence        -> _check_parent_sequence
  _validate_section_report_ids     -> _check_section_report_ids
  _validate_availability_condition -> _check_availability_condition
  _validate_groupby_no_child       -> _check_groupby_no_child
  _validate_groupby                -> _check_groupby
  _validate_engine                 -> _check_engine

account_reports carries the one override, _check_groupby, renamed with them; the
gate does not measure that repo (§9.4), so it contributes nothing to either number.
